catalog_locator: printed p. 60 (PDF p. 63), cap. 6 'A grafia do Akwê Xakriabá', sec. 6.1 'A lista de Martius: possíveis diferenças entre Xakriabá e Xerente', item D 'Registro gráfico de vogais nasais'
catalog_quote: Sugiro que a nasalidade das vogais nasais seja representada pelo til sobre as vogais: ã, ẽ, ĩ, õ e ũ. Assim, a palavra homem passaria a ser grafada como <ãba>. Como o acento em Xakriabá é geralmente na última sílaba, é desnecessário usar o acento agudo na vogal tônica.

new_statements.quote: Sugiro que a nasalidade das vogais nasais seja representada pelo til sobre as vogais: ã, ẽ, ĩ, õ e ũ. Assim, a palavra homem passaria a ser grafada como <ãba>. Como o acento em Xakriabá é geralmente na última sílaba, é desnecessário usar o acento agudo na vogal tônica.
new_statements.translation: I suggest that the nasality of nasal vowels be represented by a tilde over the vowels: ã, ẽ, ĩ, õ and ũ. Thus the word for 'man' would come to be written <ãba>. Since the accent (stress) in Xakriabá is generally on the last syllable, it is unnecessary to use the acute accent on the stressed vowel.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: URL live (HEAD 200, Content-Length 1086210 = mirror copy, 80 pp; title page: UFMG FaE, FIEI hab. LAL, Liliane Rodrigues Mota, orientador Carlo Sandro de Oliveira Campos, Outubro de 2020). Quote found verbatim in the mirror at lines 2317-2320, on the page headed 60 (PDF p. 63; the item-D heading starts at the foot of p. 59), inside cap. 6 'A grafia do Akwê Xakriabá', sec. 6.1 'A lista de Martius: possíveis diferenças entre Xakriabá e Xerente' — locator correct. Context read (ch. 6 intro, items A-E, J, closing 'acentos' remarks): the sentence 'Como o acento em Xakriabá é geralmente na última sílaba, é desnecessário usar o acento agudo na vogal tônica' is an orthographic rationale about the Xa…
new_statements.relation_note: Ch. 6 also gives the Xerente phoneme inventory (after Cotrim 2016) as the reference for Akwẽ-Xakriabá spelling, CV~CCV correspondences (Xakriabá tika : Xerente tka), k~g voicing, s/z ~ ʃ/ʒ, final e~i; no tone.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress generally falls on the final syllable (hence the acute accents on final vowels in the 19th-century lists, e.g. ambá 'man', are redundant and dropped in the proposed orthography).
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged with 'geralmente' (generally); no exceptions listed. Elsewhere (item J, p. 63) the author keeps an acute or diaeresis only to mark open-mid vowel quality [ɛ] (amyõtxé/amyõtxë, kuteté), not stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Author is a Xakriabá teacher (TI Xakriabá, São João das Missões, MG); the object is the historical Xakriabá of the Eschwege/Saint-Hilaire/Martius lists (xakr1238, Central Jê) plus the community's present-day 'Akwẽ-Xakriabá' school vocabulary, which mixes remembered items with Xerente (xere1240) loans. The stress remark is made in sec. 6.1 'A lista de Martius', i.e. about the Xakriabá forms as recorded (ambá etc.), not about Xerente. File was already in the held dir from a 2026-09-19 lexical pass (not read for stress); not in the stress-catalog bibliography.

sources.note: Only: '..le village de Santa-Anna, habité par des Indiens Chicriabas, dont la langue, si j'en juge par le peu de mots que j'ai pu recueillir, doit être éminemment systématique, puisque ceux de ces mots qui représentent des idées de même nature commencent ou finissent par une même syllabe.' — a morphological observation (shared possessive prefix/classifier syllables), nothing on accent. The same phrase recurs in his 1848 note to the Académie (Comptes rendus 26, 29 May 1848: 'la langue étonnamment systématique des Chicriabas').
